_source.note: Stage 2 content. p6: 'Six word cards from the prep guide. Each flips to a plain meaning and a one-line example.' p6: 'Four quick questions, 25 points each.' p6: 'Meera links each word to the deal where it matters most.'

stage_lede: Six words you will use today.
stage_hint: Tap a card to see a real example. Then answer four quick questions.

words.meaning: The job a client gives the bank.
words.example: A retailer asks you to find and buy an online marketplace for it.

words.meaning: What a company is worth, and why.
words.example: Thirteen staff, no revenue — but thirty million users. What is that worth?
Reading a regulator letter that the seller did not mention.

words.meaning: One page with the key terms of the deal.
words.example: Stake, price, new money, and what happens to the founders.

words.meaning: Part of the price paid later, if targets are hit.
words.example: Pay 80% now and the rest if the company hits its numbers next year.

words.meaning: How well two companies help each other.
words.example: A theme park, a television channel and a toy line can all use the same characters.

questions.prompt: The job a client gives the bank — what is that called?
questions.why: The mandate is the job itself. Everything else is a tool you use while doing it.

questions.prompt: A buyer and seller cannot agree on price. Which tool pays part of the price later, only if the company does well?
questions.why: An earnout moves part of the price into the future and ties it to performance. It is how you close a gap when two sides disagree about what the company is worth.

questions.prompt: You are reading contracts, plant records and regulator letters before your client commits. What is that work called?
questions.why: Due diligence is everything you check before you commit. The deals that go wrong usually had a letter nobody read.

questions.prompt: Two companies sell to the same customers in the same cities. Why might that make a merger attractive?
questions.why: Strategic fit is how well two companies help each other. It is the reason a buyer pays more than the numbers alone would justify.

deal_book_lede: Five mandates landed on your desk.
deal_book_hint: Advise each client. Go, go with protection, or walk away. Not every deal on your desk is a good deal.
